about: How tools/blender/prop_pack.py fits each Meshy prop. yaw: degrees about the up axis that turn the model's front to -Y in Blender (+Z in the GLB); every Meshy run of 2026-11-20 already faced -Y (renders/meshy/props/<name>/raw-views.png). flip: turned upside down (the ceiling was drawn beam side up). tile: the box faces a kit module meets its neighbours with; vertices within snap_share of the module's size (at most snap_max metres) of such a face are put exactly onto it. tex: 2k keeps 2048 maps, everything else gets 1024. dark_white: near-white texels Meshy painted into closed holes become black (true, or [mean brightness above, at most this much colour]). clear: faces centred in these boxes [x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1] (fitted metres, Blender axes) are deleted. fit_height/lift/lift_top/ring: the clamp hangs from the ceiling over a plain floor ring made here.

kit_floor_grate.note: Meshy made the grate as flat slabs with the bars only painted on and the white backdrop painted into the gaps (pink and cream cells); dark_white only blackens the whitest of them. It cannot be seen through: listed for a Blender rebuild.

kit_door_frame.note: Meshy put a slanted slab into the lower left of the opening; clear deletes it. The opening is about 2.6 m wide and 5.4 m tall, a little right of centre (x -1.17 to 1.45).

kit_vent_cover.note: The kicked-open slat flap sticks out in front, so the box is 0.6 m deep instead of 0.3 m: the frame keeps its thickness and its back is flush.

clamp.note: Meshy made the hoist and the two arms; the floor ring is a plain dark steel ring added by prop_pack.py. The hoist's top is at 7 m, where it meets the ceiling.
